Article Title: US reacts to PM Modi-Iran president Pezeshkian meet; issues warning to countries 'helping' Tehran
Article Text:
File Photo: PM Modi holds a bilateral meeting with the President of Iran, Masoud Pezeshkian, on the sidelines of the SCO Summit, in Bishkek

The US has warned countries against helping Iran evade sanctions, saying those that assist Tehran in generating revenue could themselves face sanctions. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio issued the warning after Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan.Asked about the PM Modi-Pezeshkian meeting and whether India and Iran were discussing a trade deal, Rubio said, “Well, I don't think there's a trade deal between India and Iran. Obviously there are, you know, countries all develop their own foreign policy, and many countries around the world talk to the Iranian regime.”Rubio acknowledged that several countries maintain contact with Tehran but stressed that Washington would take action against countries that help Iran bypass US sanctions.“No country should be helping Iran evade sanctions. No country should be out there helping them create mechanisms by which they can generate revenue that they will then use to sponsor terrorism and try to build a nuclear weapon,” Rubio said.“And if countries decide to do that, then we're going to have to sanction them, too,” he added.PM Modi's meeting with Pezeshkian came as the Iranian president travelled to Bishkek for the SCO summit, where regional and international issues are expected to dominate discussions.Ahead of his departure, Pezeshkian said Iran did not seek war but would respond “with strength and determination” to any aggression. He also warned that instability in the region would be detrimental to all countries and called for greater cooperation on economic and security issues.“This meeting is very important and most of the leaders of the region will be present in it. In a situation where some international institutions are seeking to create a unified space in the world, this meeting is considered a symbol of the existence of diverse and independent voices in the global arena,” he said.During the meeting with Pezeshkian, Modi is expected to discuss bilateral ties and regional developments. India has consistently called for dialogue and diplomacy to resolve issues in West Asia.PM Modi had also spoken to Pezeshkian in March, when the Iranian president briefed him on developments in the region. PM Modi had stressed India's concerns over the safety of Indian nationals in the region, including Iran, as well as the need for uninterrupted transit of energy and goods.
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi met iranian president masoud pezeshkian on the sidelines of the shanghai cooperation organisation (sco) summit in bishkek, kyrgyzstan. Us secretary of state marco rubio issued the warning after the meeting.

Article Title: Ex-IAF wing commander Abhinandan Varthaman who shot down Pak jet after Balakot strikes joins private airline

Former Indian Air Force Group Captain and Vir Chakra awardee Abhinandan Varthaman has joined Goa-based regional airline FLY91 as a pilot.Varthaman, who became widely known after shooting down a Pakistani fighter during an aerial engagement in 2019 before being captured by Pakistan, joined the airline in August.His move to commercial aviation comes after a distinguished career in the IAF, including his role in the aerial combat that followed India's Balakot air strikes.On February 26, 2019, the IAF carried out an air strike on a Jaish-e-Mohammed facility in Balakot, Pakistan, days after a terrorist attack on a CRPF convoy in Pulwama killed 40 personnel.The following day, Pakistani fighter jets attempted to launch an aerial attack, prompting the IAF to scramble aircraft to intercept them.Varthaman, then a Wing Commander with the Srinagar-based 51 Squadron, was flying a MiG-21 Bison when he engaged a Pakistani F-16. The IAF said he shot down the Pakistani fighter before his own aircraft was hit.Varthaman ejected over territory controlled by Pakistan and was taken into custody by the Pakistani Army. He was released three days later following intense diplomatic and political pressure from India.He was awarded the Vir Chakra, India's third-highest wartime gallantry award, in 2021 for his actions during the aerial engagement. He was subsequently promoted to Group Captain.Also read | Balakot hero Abhinandan Varthaman conferred Vir Chakra

Article Title: Operation Sindoor commander Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra selected as Ram temple Trust’s first CEO
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lucknow: Sixteen months after Operation Sindoor, the officer who commanded India’s western air operations has been chosen for a very different responsibility. The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has selected Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra as the first Chief Executive Officer of the Ram temple in Ayodhya Speaking to TOI, Mishra said, “I came to know about my appointment via news, I’m yet to receive official communication from trust.”The decorated former Indian Air Force commander retired in April 2026 and will now oversee the temple Trust’s expanding administrative responsibilities. However, the standard operating procedure for the appointment and functioning of the CEO has not yet been finalised, said Govind Dev Giri, general secretary of the Trust.Mishra was the Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Indian Air Force’s Western Air Command when Operation Sindoor was launched on May 7, 2025, in response to the Pahalgam terror attack.Much of the air operations in four days was directed from the command rooms of the Western Air Command, one of the Air Force’s most important operational formations. Mishra oversaw decisions linked to the deployment of aircraft and air defence assets during the military response.Also read | Ram Mandir’s first CEO has a war command pedigree: Meet Air Marshal Jitendra Mishra He was among the senior military commanders recognised for leadership during Operation Sindoor. President Droupadi Murmu conferred the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal on him in recognition of his distinguished service during the operation.Mishra’s appointment brings to the Trust a senior leader with extensive experience in operational planning, coordination, logistics and managing large formations.In a recent podcast interview, Mishra spoke about the air campaign during Operation Sindoor and explained how Indian forces identified and struck targets deep inside Pakistan. He described how a target located around 314 km away was destroyed after a brief operational instruction to “shoot”.While discussing the operation, he highlighted the importance of planning, precision, technology and coordination among different arms of the armed forces. Several operational details, however, remain classified.Mishra has roots in Uttar Pradesh. He originally belongs to Bhopatpura in Deoria district, around three hours by road from Ayodhya. He comes from a middle-class family and his father was a lecturer.Mishra joined the National Defence Academy in 1983 and was commissioned as a fighter pilot in December 1986. He later qualified as an experimental test pilot, one of the most specialised roles in military aviation.During his career, he served as chief test pilot of both the Indian Air Force and Hindustan Aeronautics Limited. In the role, he flew aircraft during development and testing stages, assessing their performance and identifying technical limitations before induction and operational deployment.Following the terrorist attack on the Pathankot air base in Jan 2016, Mishra was selected to take over the station and strengthen its administration and security systems. He later commanded the Aircraft and Systems Testing Establishment in Bengaluru, which works with HAL, the Defence Research and Development Organisation and civilian scientists on aviation systems.Mishra also served for three years at Air Headquarters in New Delhi, where he handled defence procurement. He was associated with around 75 projects and led the Air Force’s role in the first emergency procurement tranche during 2019 and 2020. His professional training includes war management at the Air Command and Staff College in the United States and strategic studies at the Royal College of Defence Studies in London.The Trust’s CEO selection process began with 5,585 applications. The selection committee, headed by retired Justice Permod Kohli and comprising Lieutenant General V.K. Chaturvedi and nuclear scientist Dr Suresh Haware, conducted technology-assisted screening, verification and online assessments.The process was coordinated by the Trust secretariat under Sameer Panda.The field was eventually narrowed to 16 candidates, who were interviewed in Ayodhya on Au​g 11 and 12. A panel of three names was submitted to the Trust on Sept 1, following which Mishra was selected.As CEO, Mishra is expected to oversee the temple’s day-to-day administration, pilgrim facilities, financial arrangements, staff coordination and management of major religious events. The Trust will now finalise the CEO’s powers, responsibilities, reporting structure and service conditions before the appointment is formally operationalised.
Article Summary: The shri ram janmabhoomi teerth kshetra trust has selected air marshal jeetendra mishra as the first chief executive officer of the ram temple in ayodhya. The decorated former indian air force commander retired in april 2026 and will now oversee the temple trust’s expanding administrative responsibilities.

Article Title: '23 Silkyara 'rat miners' offer to join Nepal tunnel rescue
Article Text:
A Delhi-NCR team of "rat miners" has offered to join rescue operations in Nepal

A Delhi-NCR team of "rat miners", whose manual excavation helped rescue all 41 workers trapped in Silkyara tunnel in 2023, has offered to join rescue operations in flood-hit Nepal, where at least 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects and about 500 are believed to be inside tunnels. Nepal Army has been prioritising search and rescue operations in 19 hydropower tunnels.Anand Kansal, Pune-based volunteer coordinator for the team, has written to Indian ambassador to Nepal, seeking help in placing the miners' expertise at the disposal of Nepalese authorities."We were highly moved after seeing news and videos (of the floods)... this is one of the worst tragedies we've witnessed in recent times," he said.Floods have damaged at least 12 hydropower projects in Rasuwa and Nuwakot - four under construction, seven operational and one undergoing testing - with mud, boulders and debris blocking or collapsing sections of tunnels.The miners came into national prominence during the Nov 2023 Silkyara-Bend-Barkot tunnel operation after mechanical drilling repeatedly failed. They entered a narrow rescue pipe and manually excavated the final stretch through the debris, helping rescuers reach 41 workers after 17 days underground.A 12-member team of the miners was also deployed at the Srisailam Left Bank Canal tunnel in Telangana in Feb 2025 after a collapse trapped eight workers. They worked there alongside specialised rescue agencies in difficult, debris-filled conditions.Firoz Qureshi, who took part in the Silkyara rescue, said the team was ready to leave immediately if Nepal sought its help. "We know what those families are going through right now, waiting for word. If we can go and help, we are ready today, not tomorrow."Monu Kumar, the youngest member of the group, said their manual techniques could be useful where heavy machinery was unable to penetrate. "Our hands and our tools can go where big machines cannot," he said. "We just need permission to go and start."

Article Title: ‘Reprehensible act of vandalism’: India condemns demolition of century-old Hindu temple in Pakistan, seeks probe
Article Text:

India flags authorities' 'apathy'

Temple's destruction triggered calls for restoration

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday expressed deep concern over reports of the destruction of a historic Hindu temple in Pakistan's Punjab province and called on the Pakistani government to conduct a prompt and transparent investigation into the incident.Responding to media queries, ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India “unequivocally” condemned the reported vandalism of the century-old place of worship in Siraj village in Narowal.“We have noted with deep concern the disturbing reports of the destruction of a historic Hindu temple in village Siraj, Narowal, Pakistan. We unequivocally condemn this reprehensible act of vandalism against a century old minority place of worship,” Jaiswal said.The MEA said the apparent failure of authorities to protect the temple was alarming and raised concerns over the safety and religious freedoms of minority communities in Pakistan.“The apparent apathy of authorities and failure to protect this century-old temple is alarming. Such incidents are a stark reminder of the continuing vulnerability of minority communities and the egregious violations of their religious freedoms and places of worship in Pakistan,” Jaiswal said.India called upon Pakistan to investigate the incident and ensure that those responsible are held accountable.“We call upon the Government of Pakistan to conduct a prompt and transparent investigation into this incident and ensure that those responsible are held fully accountable,” the MEA spokesperson said.India also urged Pakistan to take immediate steps to restore the temple and ensure the safety and security of minority communities and their cultural heritage.“Furthermore, the Government of Pakistan must take immediate remedial measures to restore the desecrated temple and fulfill its primary obligation to guarantee the safety, security and well-being of all its minority citizens and their cultural heritage,” Jaiswal added.The more than 100-year-old temple in Siraj village, around 130 km from Lahore, was demolished on August 21.Minority groups alleged that religious zealots had targeted the site to absorb its land into an adjacent madrassa, while Pakistan's Evacuee Trust Property Board (ETPB) maintained that the structure had collapsed following torrential rains.ETPB senior official Rana Iftikhar acknowledged the temple's historical significance, saying it was “more than 100 to 125 years old”, while maintaining that the land on which the temple stood had not been leased to anyone.The demolition prompted demands from minority groups and local Hindu community leaders for an investigation and the restoration of the temple.
Article Summary: The more than 100-year-old temple in siraj village, around 130 km from lahore, was demolished on august 21. NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar will travel to Ukraine and Poland from September 3 to 5, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Wednesday. The talks are expected to focus on bilateral ties, regional developments and issues of mutual interest.During the visit, Jaishankar will hold bilateral talks with Ukraine’s foreign minister Andrii Sybiha and Poland’s deputy prime minister and Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski.The ministry's official release stated that the visit would focus on “enhancing bilateral relations” and provide an opportunity to exchange views on “regional developments and issues of mutual interest.”The Ukraine leg comes days after Ukraine’s first deputy head of the office of the president, Sergiy Kyslytsya, held what he described as a “substantive meeting” with India’s ambassador to Ukraine Anjani Kumar.In a post on X, Kyslytsya said they discussed “prospects for Ukraine-India relations, including India's role in efforts to end Russia's war against Ukraine.”He said the meeting also covered Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent message to Russian President Vladimir Putin that “the time has come to move from an endless war to an end of war.”“We look forward to continued dialogue with India and to translating this shared interest in peace into concrete steps,” Kyslytsya said.The visit also follows the death of an Indian national in a Russian aerial attack on Ukraine. Article Title: ‘Not democratically elected’: SC says Manan Kumar Mishra only ‘pro tem’ BCI chairman till fresh election
Article Text:
​BCI chief Manan Kumar Mishra only ‘pro tem’ till fresh election, Supreme Court says​

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday said Bar Council of India (BCI) chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra was only a “pro tem Chairman” until a freshly constituted BCI elects its office-bearers, and directed that major policy decisions be taken in consultation with the Attorney General for India and the Solicitor General, who are permanent ex-officio BCI members.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said Mishra could oversee the BCI's day-to-day functioning but could not be treated as a democratically elected office-bearer once the newly elected state bar councils complete the process of constituting a fresh BCI.“You should also bear in mind that you are like a pro tem chairman till a fresh election of the Bar Council of India, pursuant to the elections already conducted in the state bar councils, takes place,” Justice Bagchi told senior advocate Guru Krishnakumar, appearing for the BCI chairman, according to LiveLaw.“So, it is not a situation where he is democratically elected and continues to be so. His term is co-terminus with the elections which are imminent,” the judge said.The court said the existing arrangement could continue for routine administrative work but stressed that institutional checks would apply to policy decisions.“In such situations, day-to-day functioning can be left to the existing arrangement. However, when a policy decision is taken, the participation of a permanent ex officio member acting independently, such as the Attorney General, is necessary,” Justice Bagchi remarked orally, PTI said.The bench also said it was not endorsing Mishra's continued tenure.“We are not placing any stamp of approval upon the existing arrangement. It is apparent that the present chairperson can continue only until a fresh election to the Bar Council of India takes place pursuant to the state bar council elections already conducted,” it said.The observations came while the court heard pleas challenging Mishra's continued occupation of the BCI chairperson's post and the legal basis for extending his tenure until 2030.Senior advocate Madhavi Divan, appearing for the petitioners, said Mishra was unanimously elected chairman for a term from April 17, 2025 to April 16, 2030. She also challenged a resolution extending the tenure of the chairman and vice-chairman from three years to five years despite rules prescribing a two-year term.Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for one of the petitioners, questioned the creation of the Bar Council of India Trust for Promotion of Education, Legal and Professional Reforms and Improvement in Research.Sankaranarayanan alleged that its deed made 11 managing trustees “original and permanent trustees”. The bench questioned how elected members could appoint themselves as perpetual trustees.“The Bar Council of India is a juristic entity. That entity has created a trust from its assets through the elected members who constituted the Council. Can those elected members make themselves permanent trustees of those assets when the composition of the corporate entity that settled the trust is itself determined through elections?” it asked.The court directed the newly constituted state bar councils to elect their office-bearers and representatives to the BCI within three weeks of notification of their composition. The matter will be heard next on September 23.
Article Summary: Bci chief manan kumar mishra only ‘pro tem’ till fresh election, supreme court says. Justices joymalya bagchi and v mohana said mishra could oversee the bci's day-to-day functioning but could not be treated as a democratically elected office-bearer.

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde criticised Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ’s Office for cropping Prime Minister Narendra Modi out of a photograph from the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit, saying Pakistan should not attempt to “play such games” with India.“What Pakistan has done is extremely unfortunate. Pakistan has always attempted such things. However, I would say that while they may have removed Modi Ji’s photograph, if Modi Ji wants, he can remove Pakistan from the world picture,” Shinde said on Tuesday.His remarks came after Sharif’s office shared an edited version of the SCO family photograph that placed the Pakistani prime minister at the centre while cropping out several leaders. Therefore, Pakistan should never attempt to play such games with our country,” Shinde added.He also said that editing Modi out of the photograph would not affect his standing in India or internationally.“I would also say that such an act of removing a photograph cannot erase Prime Minister Modi from the hearts of 140 crore Indians. Article Title: SC: Why not use 'totaliser' to mix votes?
Article Text:
Supreme Court Tuesday sought Centre's response to the use of a 'totaliser' mechanism to mix votes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday sought Centre's response to the use of a 'totaliser' mechanism to mix votes from different EVMs before counting, to prevent any backlash from candidates by preserving voter anonymity.Petitioner advocate Ashwini Upadhyay said a totalisation system hides booth-wise voting patterns by mixing up votes from multiple electronic voting machines (typically around 14) before displaying the count, which helps protect voters from post-poll violence and political victimisation. Election Commission , through senior advocate D Seshadri Naidu, said the issue was referred by EC to govt, which consulted stakeholders and found it inadvisable to employ the 'totalisation' mechanism, mainly because of staunch opposition by political parties. He said a switch to this method would require changing the statute which the commission could not bring about.When Upadhyay pointed out that the totalisation mechanism was adopted by EC to count paper ballots, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked Centre to respond on why the same mechanism could not be adopted for EVMs. Upadhyay also said in Jan 2018, EC itself had told the court that the "time had come" to introduce the totaliser to "protect secrecy of the ballot and privacy of the individual".It had said that "the right of the people staying in a particular locality should not be exposed, and any kind of prejudice or discrimination because of the voting pattern should be avoided".In a U-turn, EC in its affidavit filed on Aug 31 said, "Experience of litigations has revealed that the present system which includes a simultaneous audit by the candidates is necessary to ensure that frivolous and baseless allegations do not cloud the outcome..." It said the introduction of the totaliser system would give fresh anxieties, misgivings and allegations regarding data, machine tampering and transmission glitches.
Article Summary: Supreme court tuesday sought centre's response to the use of a 'totaliser' mechanism to mix votes from different evms. Election commission said the issue was referred by ec to govt, which consulted stakeholders and found it inadvisable to employ the 'totalisation' mechanism.

NEW DELHI: Buoyed by the better-than-expected GDP growth, PM Modi on Tuesday lauded Indian economy's resilience during a period of global crises. He again pushed for swadeshi goods and urged citizens to shun overseas weddings, foreign vacations and avoid unnecessary gold purchases at a time when imports remain elevated due to high commodity prices in the wake of the West Asia conflict.His appeal against buying gold also puts to rest speculation around import duties being reviewed by govt. In fact, Centre and RBI are keeping a close watch on shipments. Since Jan, both quantity of gold and value of imports have increased. Since Modi's first appeal in May, however, there has been a drop in quantity of imports but the value of imports is rising due to higher prices, albeit at a slower pace. At $3.5 a kg, the unit value of gold was 94% higher in June, but prices have moderated to $2.8 a kg, which was 47% more than a year ago.Since Modi’s first appeal in May, gold import quantity has dropped, but import value is rising due to higher prices, albeit slower. Prices moderated to $2.8 a kg, 47% more than a year ago.While gold remains an investment option for households, higher prices have deterred consumers from buying large quantities, with recycling of old jewellery also rising, industry executives said.Modi also mounted a withering attack on LoP Rahul Gandhi for spreading pessimism about growth, dismissing his criticism as “jhooth ki goonj”.This was Modi’s second reaction to the growth rate within 24 hours. His message mixed praise for people’s hard work with disdain for critics like Rahul and reiterated his call to citizens to avoid non-essential gold purchases and foreign trips.“We have to maintain this pace and keep growing and, for this, aatmanirbhar Bharat is essential,” he said in a selfie-video posted on Instagram.GDP grew at 7.8% in the April-June quarter, bringing relief to the NDA govt, which has been buffeted by the opposition parties, especially Congress under Rahul, over alleged misgovernance. Modi said, “There are people within India who are mired in despair, ‘jhooth ki goonj’, and are busy spreading pessimism everywhere.”Emphasising India’s feat, Modi said it came amid global conflicts and crises, causing supply-chain disruption. Since Covid in 2020, stability has remained elusive for the world but India is progressing at a fast pace, he added.Opposition has a right to criticise govt but especially Congress shouldn’t insult people by being incorrigible naysayers and call India a dead economy when data speaks otherwise, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said.BJP played up Rahul’s dismissive comments about the economy to contrast them with India’s growth. Besides his dead economy jibe, Rahul claimed a crisis unseen in people’s lifetime would hit the economy. An economic tsunami was coming, he had said. Modi said his govt’s policy is right and intentions clear, calling upon people to work hard. India’s collective strength will take it to new heights. By emphasising swadeshi and self-reliance, people will bequeath a developed India to the young generation.At a press conference, BJP’s Ravi Shankar Prakash demanded Rahul apologise. As leader of opposition, Rahul’s comments carry weight, he said. The world has begun taking them lightly as he makes misleading remarks, while Pakistan plays them up.
Article Summary: Pm modi on tuesday lauded indian economy's resilience during a period of global crises. He again pushed for swadeshi goods and urged citizens to shun overseas weddings, foreign vacations and avoid unnecessary gold purchases. Since modi's first appeal in may, there has been a drop in quantity of imports but the value of imports is rising due to higher prices, albeit slower.

Article Title: Pak takes SCO chair, PM Modi slams use of terror as strategic asset
Article Text:
Modi said countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy must be sent a strong message

Also Read:

Framing security as a non-negotiable prerequisite for regional progress, PM Narendra Modi delivered a thinly veiled warning to Pakistan over state-sponsored terrorism at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. With Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif in attendance, Modi said countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy, and provide shelter and support to terrorists, must be sent a strong message that terrorism can never be a strategic asset for anyone.The remarks are significant also because of the timing. Pakistan assumed rotating chairmanship of SCO from Kyrgyzstan on Tuesday and will host the heads-of-state summit next year, for which it will invite Modi, along with others.Modi made the remarks, in which he also warned against double standards on terrorism, while expanding on India's SCO vision - Security, Connectivity and Opportunity - that he articulated in Tianjin last year.With Chinese President Xi Jinping also present, PM reiterated India's position that all connectivity initiatives must respect sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states as this is also the "fundamental spirit" of SCO charter.Modi said that terrorism continued to pose a serious challenge to humanity and it's important to not remain confined to an action-reaction approach in the fight against the menace.“We must dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorist financing, recruitment, radicalisation, and safe havens. We must speak with one voice and make it clear that there can be no place for double standards on this serious issue,” said PM, without naming Pakistan as SCO charter doesn’t allow members to raise bilateral differences.India and Pakistan together joined the China-dominated Eurasian grouping as full members in 2017. For India, the security-oriented SCO has served as a platform not just to assert its strategic autonomy but also flag regional risks from state-sponsored terrorism. Modi said that the bloc’s shared aspiration for a peaceful and secure Eurasia is also closely linked to peace and stability in Afghanistan and that India will continue to contribute to the development and provision of humanitarian assistance to people of the country.Modi addressed West Asia crisis, saying it was affecting energy security, maritime trade and supply chains around the world and recalling his message earlier that conflicts cannot be resolved on the battlefield. “Countries of Global South bear greatest brunt of such disruptions. Therefore, India has consistently called for all tensions and conflicts to be resolved not on battlefield, but through dialogue and diplomacy,” he added.While underlining the importance India attaches to SCO, Modi said that at a time when the world is passing through instability, the organisation must transform the shared geography into opportunities and bring about positive change in people’s lives. Describing SCO as a confluence of great civilisations, cultures, and ideas, he said that over next 25 years, people-to-people ties should remain at the heart of cooperation among the member states.“True measure of our success should be how many new opportunities our efforts create, how many new markets open up for entrepreneurs, how much farmers benefit from tech, and how much better the lives of our citizens become,” said the PM. According to an Indian readout of PM’s participation, Modi stated that strong and trusted connectivity initiatives were important for the group’s shared progress and prosperity.“Underlining that India supports connectivity efforts that link markets, enhance trade and open new opportunities for development, he reiterated such efforts should respect sovereignty and territorial integrity of nations,” said the readout.
Article Summary: Modi said countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy must be sent a strong message. Pakistan assumed rotating chairmanship of sco from kyrgyzstan on tuesday. India and pakistan together joined the china-dominated eurasian grouping as full members in 2017.

Article Title: US struck 60 targets as 40 vessels, 18mn barrels of oil crossed Hormuz in record day: Report
Article Text:
The operation comes amid growing risks for commercial shipping

The US military escorted 40 commercial vessels carrying around 18 million barrels of oil through the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, marking a wartime high as Washington and Tehran exchanged a fresh round of strikes, according to two US officials familiar with the operation who spoke to CNN.The high-risk operation came as US forces simultaneously struck nearly 60 Iranian military targets around the strategic waterway, while defending the escorted vessels against waves of drone attacks and neutralising anti-ship cruise missiles.Before the war began just over six months ago, around 20 million barrels of oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz each day. But since the conflict began, shipping through the key waterway has slowed to a trickle, disrupting global energy markets and pushing up prices.The US operation involved a range of air, sea and space assets and was part of a broader strategy focused on controlling the strait, protecting commercial shipping and increasing economic pressure on Iran.The targets hit on Tuesday included air defence sites, radar systems, maritime assets, mine-laying capabilities and communications sites, the officials told CNN. US forces also continued a naval blockade of Iranian ports, with Central Command directed to focus its efforts on the strait and preventing oil exports from leaving or entering Iranian ports.The operation comes amid growing risks for commercial shipping. On Monday, a Saudi Arabia-flagged crude oil tanker came under attack and caught fire as it was preparing to cross the strait, killing two Filipino crew members. Fourteen other Filipino crew members survived.Iran has also stepped up attacks on US allies in the Gulf. Bahrain said its air defence systems intercepted several Iranian air attacks early Wednesday, while Iranian state media reported drone attacks on US bases in Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates.The escalation followed US strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday. Washington said Iran was preparing to use the launchers to fire mines into the waterway. Iran retaliated by launching missiles at American bases in Jordan, which were intercepted.The US military’s latest operation, however, has not eased concerns among energy companies about sending ships through the strait, even under military escort. Energy prices remain elevated, adding to turbulence in global markets.At the same time, the administration’s other priorities have taken a back seat. According to one US official, operations aimed at eliminating elements of Iran’s nuclear programme have effectively been “backburnered”, as the focus shifts towards securing the waterway and restricting Iranian oil flows.Iranian media meanwhile reported that a US strike hit a home hosting a wedding in Kuhestak, killing four people and wounding at least 68. The US military said it was aware of the report but that it “never targets civilians.”With the conflict intensifying, diplomatic efforts are continuing. Egypt and Qatar have called for Washington and Tehran to return to negotiations, while Pakistan said it remains engaged in mediation efforts. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also said Washington was pressuring countries still doing business with Iran, saying, “My message to everyone is stay away.”
Article Summary: The us military escorted 40 commercial vessels carrying around 18 million barrels of oil through the strait of hormuz on tuesday. The high-risk operation came as us forces simultaneously struck nearly 60 iranian military targets around the strategic waterway.

Article Title: Nepal flash floods: Relatives hold symbolic funerals for thousands missing as toll crosses 1,243
Article Text:
The death toll from devastating flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet region rose to 1,243 on Thursday.

The death toll from devastating flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet region rose to 1,243 on Thursday, as rescue teams battled heavy rain and thick debris while searching for people believed to be trapped in tunnels and underground power facilities along the Bhotekoshi River.Prime Minister Balendra Shah said Nepal must raise the disaster’s connection to climate change with the international community, as families held symbolic funerals for relatives who remain missing following last week’s floods.Speaking at the fifth daily press briefing in Kathmandu, ministry of foreign affairs spokesperson Lok Bahadur Chhetri said authorities had begun conducting temporary burials for victims as search and rescue operations continued around the clock.Chhetri said 11,993 people had been rescued, while 1,114 bodies had been recovered. Around 3,900 people remain unaccounted for, he said, urging relatives of those missing to provide DNA samples at the Nepal Police Hospital in Maharajgunj or their nearest District Police Office to help forensic teams with identification.He also outlined international assistance being provided to Nepal. A 19-member forensic team from India is working with Nepal Police on DNA analysis, while specialised teams and equipment have also arrived from China, Singapore and South Korea to support identification and recovery efforts.Rescue teams from the Nepali Army, Nepal Police and Armed Police Force are working with international specialists from India, China and South Korea to clear mud, debris and boulders from underground hydropower facilities in areas including Langtang, Chilime and Upper Trisuli.According to the ANI report, more than 300 foreign nationals have been safely rescued, while around 590 citizens from 34 countries remain unaccounted for.Working with Chinese authorities, Nepal has also helped evacuate about 2,500 pilgrims returning from Mount Kailash through the Hilsa and Tatopani border crossings and via air routes through Lhasa. Efforts are also underway to clear stranded cargo and assist Nepali nationals near the Kerung border.Addressing Parliament earlier Wednesday, Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the catastrophic August 26 Bhotekoshi River floods, triggered by a high-altitude Himalayan avalanche, underscored the growing threat posed by climate change across the region.Shah said nearly 4,000 people remain missing across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading, stressing that addressing the effects of climate change requires a collective global effort.As Nepal continues to coordinate international assistance from India, China, the United States, Japan, the Asian Development Bank, the World Bank, the European Union and the United Nations, authorities are deploying available resources toward emergency relief, searches for missing people and long-term recovery.According to Nepal Police, 348 bodies were recovered in Chitwan, 217 in Nawalparasi East, 190 in Nawalparasi West and 155 in Nuwakot. Another 66 bodies were recovered in Gorkha, 59 in Dhading, 45 in Rasuwa and 38 in Tanahu.A total of 7,912 police personnel have been deployed to flood-hit areas to assist with search and rescue operations, distribute relief supplies and manage recovered bodies.Authorities have also published details of 911 unidentified bodies on the Nepal Police website to help families identify missing relatives.Meanwhile, rainwater accumulating inside a hydropower tunnel has created additional difficulties for search and rescue teams working in areas affected by the Bhotekoshi floods, said Dharma Raj Uprety, executive chief of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA).Search operations have been particularly challenging because of the hazardous conditions inside the project’s tunnels. Teams from the Nepali Army and Armed Police Force, along with foreign technical experts and project employees, are continuing efforts to locate workers who remain missing.As per the PTI report, Ganesh Karki, former president of the Independent Power Producers’ Association, Nepal (IPPAN), said rescue operations have also been slowed by difficulties transporting heavy equipment to the tunnels.
Article Summary: The death toll from devastating flash floods in the nepal-tibet region rose to 1,243 on thursday. Rescue teams battled heavy rain and thick debris while searching for people believed to be trapped in tunnels and underground power facilities. Prime minister balendra shah said nepal must raise the disaster’s connection to climate change with the international community.

Article Title: Trump’s face debuts on US currency, $1 coins run ‘out of stock’ within hours
Article Text:
Trump’s face debuts on US currency, $1 coins run ‘out of stock’ within hours

Trump coin out of stock

Special law for Trump's portrait

It’s America’s 250th birthday, and Donald Trump is making sure he gets a spot on the souvenir.A new $1 coin marking the anniversary went on sale Wednesday with the president’s portrait on one side and the Great Seal of the United States on the other.The coins, issued by the US mint, can be used as legal tender. But their launch has also attracted criticism because federal law bars the depiction of a living president on US currency, although there are provisions allowing the Treasury Secretary to authorise special coins in certain circumstances.The coin’s design features Trump’s visage as “heads”, while the Great Seal of the United States serves as “tails”. Trump’s portrait carries the inscriptions “IN GOD WE TRUST” and “LIBERTY”, while “1776 (tilde) 2026” appears below his face.The reverse shows the Great Seal, with a bald eagle holding arrows in one claw and an olive branch in the other. A banner held in its beak carries the words “E PLURIBUS UNUM," Latin for "out of many, one.”The design received approval this year from the US Commission of Fine Arts, whose members were appointed by Trump. The president had earlier called the idea of putting his face on a coin “very unusual”, but said he was “honored by it.”The US mint said the coins were struck to “honor 250 years of great American heritage.”The coins went on sale at noon Wednesday, but appeared to be out of stock by the afternoon.A roll of 25 coins costs $61, while a bag of 100 costs $154.50. At the same time, some special-issue coins had been randomly placed among the rolls and bags.The mint’s website later stated, “This item is available to be ordered now, but it is not currently in stock. Additional inventory is being made.”The 100-coin bag was listed as unavailable, while the 25-coin roll carried the same message shortly after 3pm.Just after 12.30pm, visitors to the website were placed in a waiting area with an estimated wait time of one hour. Purchases were limited to two per household until 2pm on Thursday, with buyers given 10 minutes to complete their orders.The website also warned, “Product availability is not guaranteed.” Furthermore, the coins would also be found in circulation, with the authority urging people to "check your pocket change.”Among the coins, 250,000 have been given a special-issue “July 4th” privy mark. Mint said that these coins were randomly included in the rolls and bags because they were struck on July 4, the anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.Describing this as a “special offering”, the mint said, “250,000 Semiquincentennial President Donald J. Trump $1 Coins with a special-issue ‘July 4th’ privy mark have been randomly included in the Rolls & Bags. These coins were struck on July 4th.”Although the coin has a gold appearance, it is made from a mix of copper, zinc, manganese and nickel. Part of the additional cost of commemorative coins goes towards “organizations and projects that benefit the community”, according to the mint’s website.The use of Trump’s image on the coin comes despite US law prohibiting the display of a sitting president or living former president on US currency.In anticipation of America’s 250th anniversary, however, Congress passed the Circulating Collectible Coin Redesign Act. The legislation allows the US Treasury to mint special $1 coins to mark the event.The law also states, “No head and shoulders portrait or bust of any person, living or dead, and no portrait of a living person may be included in the design on the reverse of specified coins.”Trump’s portrait appears on the front of the coin, rather than the reverse, appearing to comply with the law.The treasury secretary also has authority in some circumstances to approve the minting and issuance of special coins.The only other time a living president was featured on a US coin was in 1926, when Calvin Coolidge appeared on a half dollar marking the 150th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, according to the mint.The coin is also part of a wider series of branding efforts associated with Trump’s second term that have become tangled up in lawsuits.These include moves to put Trump’s name on the Kennedy Center and the US Institute of Peace, as the president seeks to leave his stamp on history and Washington, DC.CNN reached out to the Treasury Department for information on the coins’ availability and the number of orders placed. It also sought information on where the surcharge money from the coins will go.
Article Summary: Trump’s face debuts on us currency, $1 coins run ‘out of stock’ within hours. Trump coin out of stock because of special law for trump's portrait. Federal law bars depiction of a living president on u.s. currency. The legislation allows the us treasury to mint special $1 coins to mark the event.

Article Title: Air India Express Varanasi-Delhi flight makes precautionary landing in Lucknow after smoke alert
Article Text:
Air India Express (File Photo)





LUCKNOW: Air India Express flight IX 1253, operating from Varanasi to Delhi, made a precautionary landing at Lucknow airport on Thursday morning after the pilots received a smoke indication from the aircraft's aft cargo compartment.According to an official source, the pilots reported that the aircraft's sensors had detected smoke in the cargo bay. They subsequently requested permission to make a precautionary landing at Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport in Lucknow.The aircraft landed safely at 8.52 am, following which the airport emergency response team reached the site and conducted a visual inspection. No smoke was observed during the inspection.The aircraft was parked at a designated stand at the airport. Passenger deplaning began at 9.02 am, and all passengers were safely evacuated from the aircraft. The passengers were deboarded to facilitate a detailed inspection of the aircraft.In a statement, Lucknow International Airport Limited (LIAL), a subsidiary of Adani Airport Holdings Limited, said all 155 passengers and crew members on board were safe."Air India Express flight IX 1253 (Varanasi–Delhi) reported a smoke indication in the aft cargo compartment and made a precautionary landing at Lucknow Airport at 0852 hrs," the airport operator said."The aircraft landed safely, following which the airport emergency response team conducted a visual inspection. No smoke was observed," it added.The aircraft remained parked at the Lucknow airport bay after the passengers were deplaned.The cause of the smoke indication was not immediately known. A detailed inspection of the aircraft and its systems is expected to determine the reason for the alert. No passenger or crew member was reported injured in the incident.
Article Summary: Air india express flight ix 1253, operating from varanasi to delhi, made a precautionary landing. Pilots received a smoke indication from the aircraft's aft cargo compartment. All 155 passengers and crew members on board were safe. No passenger or crew member was reported injured in the incident.

Article Title: ‘Mayday emergency’: IndiGo Doha-Bengaluru flight diverts to Muscat after pilot falls ill mid-air
Article Text:
IndiGo flight (Representative image)





MUMBAI: An IndiGo flight from Doha to Bengaluru was diverted to Muscat on Thursday after one of its pilots was reportedly incapacitated mid-flight, prompting the aircraft to declare a Mayday emergency, said sources.The A320neo aircraft operating flight 6E 1302 took off from Doha at 3am, about an hour behind schedule, according to data from a flight-tracking website. Less than two hours later, the aircraft turned towards Muscat to carry out an approach and landing.Pilot incapacitation is treated as a serious in-flight emergency, as it means one of the pilots becomes unable to continue performing their duties. Aircraft such as those in the Airbus A320 family are operated by two pilots on the flight deck. If one becomes incapacitated, the other pilot can continue flying the aircraft.However, this would mean single-handedly managing all the duties normally shared between the two pilots on the flight deck, including flying and monitoring the aircraft, navigating, communicating with air traffic control, managing the aircraft’s systems and responding to abnormal or emergency situations.Since this can significantly increase the workload on the remaining pilot, pilot incapacitation is treated as an emergency.It can prompt the crew to divert to a suitable nearby airport, where the incapacitated pilot can receive medical attention and the flight can continue with a replacement crew.In a statement, IndiGo confirmed that the diversion was necessitated by an urgent requirement for medical attention for one operating crew member. The crew member was attended to by a medical team after landing and was reported to be feeling better, the airline added.The airline said an alternate aircraft and a new set of crew had been arranged to continue the journey to Bengaluru. Passengers waiting at Muscat were being provided refreshments and regular updates, it said.
Article Summary: Indigo flight from doha to bengaluru was diverted to muscat on thursday. One of its pilots was reportedly incapacitated mid-flight, prompting the aircraft to declare a mayday emergency. The crew member was attended to by a medical team after landing and was reported to be feeling better.
